subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding visual storytelling and composition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
project_brief: Create a visual narrative or series with a process journal and artist statement. This is the grade 7 culminating project for "Visual Storytelling and Composition" (ma-g7-arts-and-music-u01, unit 1), built around composition and focal point, value color and mood, perspective and depth, symbol and visual metaphor, and sequential art. Create a visual narrative or series with a process journal and artist statement. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering composition and focal point, value color and mood, perspective and depth, and symbol and visual metaphor.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: composition and focal point, value color and mood, perspective and depth, symbol and visual metaphor, sequential art, and critique and revision.
Meet the performance task as written: Create a visual narrative or series with a process journal and artist statement.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Create a visual narrative or series with a process journal and artist statement. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering composition and focal point, value color and mood, perspective and depth, and symbol and visual metaphor.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to composition and focal point or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.
Every interpretive claim about the work is backed by a specific, quoted or cited piece of evidence from the work or its context, not a general impression.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on composition and focal point, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores value color and mood from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
